mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined in each of the last four weeks with an accelerating weekly drop (-0.9, -4.1, -5.0). This momentum reflects ongoing suppression of discretionary outings and will persist without a visible structural break, pushing the next-4-week mean further below the last-4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact: RETAIL_REC fell from -34.7 to -44.7 over the last four weeks with increasing weekly decrements
failure_condition: If the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is higher than the last-28-day mean despite the observed accelerating decline, the momentum-continuation mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has fallen steeply each week (-42.6 to -52.6). If TRANSIT drops more than 5 points week-on-week again, it signals renewed mobility restrictions or public caution that will further suppress retail and recreation visits over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact: TRANSIT declined from -42.6 to -52.6 over the snapshot period, a 10-point drop
failure_condition: If TRANSIT continues to fall by more than 5 points weekly but RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next two weeks, the threshold mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of falling WORKPLACES (-27.0 to -38.0) and rising RESIDENTIAL (5.0 to 6.6) indicates a behavioral shift toward home-centered routines. When both trends co-occur, households substitute non-essential retail trips with home-based activity, compounding the depression of RETAIL_REC beyond what either series predicts alone.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES declines and RESIDENTIAL rises in the same week
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES fell 11 points while RESIDENTIAL rose 1.6 points over four weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL continue to move in this joint pattern but RETAIL_REC's next-4-week mean rises relative to the prior 4 weeks, the interaction hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous, synchronized decline across RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES suggests an active policy tightening regime (e.g., reinstated restrictions) rather than organic behavioral drift. Under this regime, RETAIL_REC will continue to fall over the next four weeks until policy signals reverse.
evidence_refs: fact: all five non-residential categories declined in every week of the snapshot
failure_condition: If any of WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, or PARKS show a rebound of more than 5 points in the coming weeks while RETAIL_REC also declines, the policy-regime explanation is undermined; outright rejection occurs if RETAIL_REC rises despite continued declines elsewhere.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility fell sharply (-4.7 to -22.0) during a summer period when seasonal outdoor demand would normally sustain or increase park visits. This counter-seasonal drop implies an overriding suppressive force; if that force weakens even briefly, a seasonal rebound in PARKS could spill over into renewed short-term retail and recreation trips within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rebounds more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS declined 17.3 points over four weeks despite the summer season
failure_condition: If PARKS rebounds by more than 5 points in a week but RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week, the seasonal spillover hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has declined less steeply (-20.3 to -30.4) than RETAIL_REC (-34.7 to -44.7), indicating selective behavioral avoidance where essential trips are preserved while discretionary retail trips are cut disproportionately. This widening gap signals continued consumer caution that will keep RETAIL_REC depressed relative to essential mobility over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: the gap between RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM widened from -14.4 to -14.3 points but both series show steeper weekly declines in RETAIL_REC
failure_condition: If the gap between RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM narrows while RETAIL_REC's next-4-week mean rises, the selective-avoidance mechanism is rejected.

failure_condition: If WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC does not decline in the following week, the rapid-spillover hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restriction regime, the combination of falling TRANSIT and rising RESIDENTIAL together reflects compounded mobility suppression: reduced transit use indicates fewer outbound trips, while rising residential time indicates more home confinement. When both signals move in this reinforcing direction simultaneously, RETAIL_REC is pulled down faster than either series would predict alone, over a two-week horizon.
